summary: Learn practical ergonomics, RULA, REBA, and workstation redesign methods. Improve employee health and reduce MSD risk. Enrol now.
lede: Ergonomics and workplace design use human factors to assess risks and shape tasks, tools, and workspaces around people. For health and safety, facilities, HR, occupational health, and industrial engineering professionals, the course supports practical workstation and workflow improvements. Learners practice RULA and REBA posture assessment, review manual handling and workstation layouts, select controls, and prepare risk registers and improvement reports.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who manage workplace conditions, employee health, or physical work design and need practical ergonomic tools they can use immediately.
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of workplace safety, operations, or facilities processes. Prior experience in occupational health and safety, HR, facilities management, industrial engineering, or line supervision is helpful, but not required. No coding or programming is required. An intermediate level is appropriate for professionals who already observe workplace conditions and want to assess ergonomic risk, build workstation improvement plans, and use tools such as RULA, REBA, and ergonomic checklists with confidence.
